title: However God works in free causes, he leaves them the power to act otherwise
source_text: LIX. Nec minus apud me certum est, quocunque modo Deus in causis liberis agat & operetur, id facere semper ipsarum naturae congruenter, nec quicquam libertati earum praejudicare: ac proinde quum voluntates humanas ad hunc aut illum actum efficaciter movet, ab iis non tollere potestatem aliter agendi.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is it less certain with me, that in whatever way God acts and operates in free causes, he does it always congruently with their nature, nor prejudices their liberty in anything: and therefore when he efficaciously moves human wills to this or that act, he does not take from them the power of acting otherwise.
pass_b_english: I am no less certain that, in whatever way God acts and works in free causes, he always does so in keeping with their nature and without any prejudice to their freedom.
So when he efficaciously moves human wills to one act or another, he does not take from them the power to act otherwise.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
